title: Replies to Critics
version: Disputatio 13(63), 445–494 (2021 issue; ResearchGate page lists April 2023); DOI 10.2478/disp-2021-0026; accessible author text in ResearchGate full-text HTML
locator: Selected full-text reading of §8, printed pp. 482–486; key explanandum-fact/explanans-fact distinction on p. 484. HTML text and printed page markers inspected; PDF page images not inspected.
assumptions: Authors' reply to Dorato and Hoefer on bivalent future contingents under growing-block theory; their proposed non-orthodox truth-grounding requirement and distinction between present truth facts and later explanatory facts.
conclusion: Authors say the present fact that a future claim Q is true is the explanandum fact and exists now, while the truth now of a sentence describing its grounding does not entail that the embedded because-claim or corresponding explanans fact exists now. The future event/fact may serve as explanans when it exists later; some present facts obtain only courtesy of what will but may not yet exist.
proof_status: Philosophical reply; selected primary passages read, not a formal proof audit or validation of the grounding account.
dependencies: Correia and Rosenkranz, Nothing to Come (2018), chapter 7, invoked by the reply but not read in this task
Dorato and Hoefer (2021), critique answered in §8; not read in this task
open_questions: Does the authors' account apply without modification to the scalar-field proposition used in the project model?
What account of derivative present truth facts and later grounding makes the explanation adequate?
How does the full quantified tense logic constrain the selected §8 proposal?
relevance: Directly bears on whether criticism confuses an existing present explanandum truth-fact with a future explanans, and on whether equal intrinsic field-past data imply equal complete current reality.
limits: Selected full-text scope only: §8 pp. 482–486, especially p. 484. ResearchGate accessible HTML text and page markers inspected; PDF images, the full book chapter 7, full critic paper, and complete quantified tense logic not audited. Does not establish that the project’s simplified Contract L reproduces the authors’ full view or that their grounding account succeeds.
